title: Flamiche
subtitle: A French leek tart in a rich shortcrust case from Picardy
excerpt: Soft buttered leeks in a creamy egg filling baked in a shortcrust case. A simple, deeply savoury tart that works as a starter or a light main.
sourceNotes: Traditional tart from Picardy and Burgundy in northern France.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the baked tart in slices. Reheat from frozen in a 180C oven for 15 minutes until hot through.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cook the leeks up to two days ahead and refrigerate. The baked tart keeps in the fridge for two days.

content.text: Flamiche relies on leeks cooked slowly in butter until very soft and sweet. The filling is simple: egg, cream, and the leeks. Blind-bake the case first so the base stays crisp under the wet filling.

items.prepNote: white and pale green parts, sliced into rounds

content.text: Roll the pastry on a lightly floured surface to 3mm thick. Line a 23cm loose-bottomed tart tin. Press into the edges, trim the overhang, and chill for 30 minutes.

Heat the oven to 190C. Line the pastry case with baking paper and fill with baking beans. Blind-bake for 15 minutes. Remove the paper and beans and bake for a further 5 minutes until pale gold. Set aside.
Melt the butter in the frying pan over a low heat. Add the leeks and a pinch of salt. Cook for 15 minutes, stirring often, until very soft but not coloured. Leave to cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs, double cream, and creme fraiche together. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Spread the leeks over the base of the pastry case. Pour the cream mixture over the top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes at 190C until the filling is just set with a slight wobble in the centre. It will firm as it cools.
Leave to rest for 10 minutes before slicing. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.cause: The blind-bake was too short, or the leeks went in warm.
items.fix: Bake the empty case until the base looks dry and pale gold. Cool the leeks before spooning them in.

items.cause: The oven was too hot or the tart baked too long.
items.fix: Check at 25 minutes. The centre should still wobble when you shake the tin gently.

items.symptom: The pastry shrinks down the sides.
items.cause: The dough was not rested before baking, or it was stretched too thin.
items.fix: Always chill the lined tin for at least 30 minutes and let the pastry overhang the rim before trimming.
